title: $d$-wave superconductivity in quintuple-layer bulk superconductor La$_6$Ni$_5$O$_{12}$
authors: Zhan Wang, Yuxin Wang, Hui-Ke Jin, Kun Jiang, Jiangping Hu
abstract: The recent realization of bulk superconductivity in the quintuple-layer nickelate La$_6$Ni$_5$O$_{12}$ opens new opportunities to probe the pairing symmetry of the reduced Ruddlesden--Popper (RP) nickelate family. Using an effective five-layer Hubbard model and variational Monte Carlo calculations, we find that a spin-singlet $d_{x^2-y^2}$-wave state is energetically favored, while extended-$s$-wave pairing is strongly suppressed. Based on the optimized superconducting state, we further calculate several experimentally accessible observables. The tunneling density of states exhibits a characteristic V-shaped low-energy spectrum, the superfluid density shows a linear low-temperature depletion, the Knight shift decreases below $T_c$, and the spin-lattice relaxation rate follows $1/T_1T\propto T^2$, together providing consistent signatures of a clean nodal superconductor. Extending the same framework to related reduced RP nickelates, we find a robust $d$-wave tendency in infinite-layer LaNiO$_{2}$, while trilayer La$_4$Ni$_3$O$_{8}$ at its nominal filling lies close to the boundary between $d$-wave superconductivity and a non-superconducting state. These results establish bulk La$_6$Ni$_5$O$_{12}$ as a promising platform for determining the pairing symmetry of nickelate superconductors and suggest a common $d_{x^2-y^2}$-wave pairing tendency across the reduced RP nickelate family.
summary: This theoretical study investigates the superconducting pairing symmetry in bulk nickelate superconductors using advanced Variational Monte Carlo methods. The authors find strong evidence for a d_{x^2-y^2}-wave pairing state in La6Ni5O12, supported by consistent predictions for several measurable physical quantities. This establishes the material as a key platform for understanding high-temperature superconductivity in layered nickelates.
main_problem: To determine the superconducting pairing symmetry in the reduced Ruddlesden-Popper (RP) nickelate family, using bulk superconductors as a platform.
main_result: Variational Monte Carlo calculations strongly favor a spin-singlet d_{x^2-y^2}-wave superconducting state in La6Ni5O12, suggesting a common d-wave pairing tendency across the family.
method: Variational Monte Carlo (VMC) calculations are employed using a Gutzwiller-projected wave function to minimize the energy of various superconducting ansatzes.
model_or_system: The study models the system using an effective five-layer Hubbard model for the Ni d_{x^2-y^2} sector, comparing results across La6Ni5O12, La4Ni3O8, and LaNiO2.
key_observables: Tunneling density of states (V-shaped), superfluid density (linear low-T depletion), Knight shift (decreases below Tc), and spin-lattice relaxation rate (1/T1T proportional to T^2).
important_parameters: The calculations are performed at specific hole doping levels and utilize parameters derived from the Hubbard model Hamiltonian.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the effective Hubbard model and the variational approximation inherent in VMC calculations.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the crystal structures of the nickelates and show theoretical predictions for key superconducting signatures like the density of states and superfluid density.
paper_structure: The paper systematically applies VMC to compare d-wave and s-wave pairing symmetries, calculates multiple experimental signatures based on the optimized state, and extends the findings to related nickelate compounds.
why_interesting: The detailed calculation of multiple, distinct experimental signatures (like the T-dependence of the Knight shift or relaxation rate) provides a robust theoretical benchmark for identifying unconventional pairing symmetries in correlated materials.

The corresponding nominal Ni configu- rations are d9, d8.8, and d8.67, giving hole concentrations x = 0, 0.2, and 1/3 relative to d9, respectively. Superconductivity has been es- tablished in hole-doped infinite-layer thin films [1], with onset tem- peratures approaching 40 K in Sm-based compounds [6, 7], and in bulk 6512 [40], whereas signatures have also been reported in 438 single crystals [43].
